title.rendered: Declaring Over Your Household: As For Me and My House | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 9

excerpt.rendered: Joshua chose for his whole house, and Paul promised salvation to a jailer’s family. Day 9 teaches believers how to declare like a covenant head.

content.rendered:
Joshua did not wait for a vote. He opened his mouth, made a decision for the whole house, and left it on the record of heaven.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, October 26, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 9

Today’s Scripture

“And if it seems evil to you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.”
Joshua 24:15 (NKJV)

“So they said, ‘Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.’”
Acts 16:31 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Joshua 24:15 is one of the most quoted verses on refrigerators around the world, and one of the most under-prayed verses in private rooms. The NKJV says, “as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” The AMPC renders it with its full force: “But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” The TPT rendering of Acts 16:31 is tender: “Believe on the Lord Jesus and you will experience salvation for you and your entire household.” Scripture consistently treats households as a unit, not because every family member’s choice is removed, but because God honours a believing head who stands in the gap.

Across Lagos and London, Manila and Nairobi and São Paulo, there are believers crying for prodigal spouses, prodigal sons and daughters, siblings far from the Lord, parents who have not yet surrendered. Our temptation is to argue. Our calling is to declare. The battle for the household is first fought in the mouth of the one who truly believes. Joshua did not ask his wife and children to vote. He announced. He put the decision on the public record of his family. He trusted the Lord to work it out.

Jesus took the same posture when He raised Jairus’s daughter; He put the mourners outside and spoke to the child (Mark 5:40–41). He addressed the household air before He addressed the household member. Declaration over your family does not mean controlling your family. It means standing in your God-given place and inviting heaven to run through your home as it ran through Noah’s ark, Rahab’s window, and Cornelius’s living room.

So declare it. Over the breakfast table before anyone comes down. In your car before the school run. In the compound before the neighbours wake. In the diaspora flat when the Wi-Fi is still asleep. Call out your household by name, member by member, and ask the Lord to run through your lineage. The God of Joshua, the God of the Philippian jailer, the God of the New Covenant; He has not changed. “For the promise is to you and to your children” (Acts 2:39).

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. God honours covenant heads. Your position in your family is a spiritual office. The devil would love for you to resign from it; do not.

Personalise. Name every member of your household in prayer and declaration, spouse, child, parent, sibling, in-law, long-term partner-in-faith. Hold up each name before the Lord.

Proclaim. Say it out loud: “As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Keep saying it when it looks untrue. Faith paints the mantelpiece before the furniture arrives.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that I am a believing head over my household. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. I believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and the promise of salvation is for me and my entire household. I stand in the gap for every member of my family by name. I bind every demonic strategy against my spouse, my children, my parents, my siblings, and I loose the ministry of the Holy Spirit in each one of their lives. My home is a sanctuary. My home is a lighthouse. My home is a landing strip for angels. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
